a1.cap: Biggest Water Tank
a1.say: Let's solve Biggest Water Tank, using the Two Pointers approach.

a1.cap: heights[i] is the height of a vertical wall at position i. Choose two walls; together with the ground they form a tank whose water level is limited by the shorter wall. Return the largest amount of water any pair can hold (width × shorter height).
a1.say: heights at i is the height of a vertical wall at position i. Choose two walls; together with the ground they form a tank whose water level is limited by the shorter wall. Return the largest amount of water any pair can hold (width times shorter height).

lines: heights[i] is the height of a vertical wall at position i. Choose two walls; together with the ground they form a tank whose water level is limited by the shorter wall. Return the largest amount of water any pair can hold (width × shorter height).

a1.cap: For example, with heights = [1,8,6,2,5,4,8,3,7], the answer is 49. Walls at 1 and 8: width 7, height 7.
a1.say: For example, with heights equals 1, 8, 6, 2, 5, 4, 8, 3, 7, the answer is 49. Walls at 1 and 8: width 7, height 7.

a1.cap: Start with the widest tank: L at the first wall and R at the last. The water is limited by the shorter wall.
Moving the taller wall inward can only shrink the width without raising the limit, so always move the shorter wall. Track the best area as you go.
Let's walk through it with heights = [1,8,6,2,5,4,8,3,7].
a1.say: Let's walk through it with heights equals 1, 8, 6, 2, 5, 4, 8, 3, 7.

a1.cap: Walls 1 and 7, width 8: area 8.
The left wall is shorter, so L moves right.
Walls 8 and 7, width 7: area 49.
The right wall is not taller, so R moves left.
Walls 8 and 3, width 6: area 18.
The right wall is not taller, so R moves left.
Walls 8 and 8, width 5: area 40.
The right wall is not taller, so R moves left.
Walls 8 and 4, width 4: area 16.
The right wall is not taller, so R moves left.
Walls 8 and 5, width 3: area 15.
The right wall is not taller, so R moves left.
Walls 8 and 2, width 2: area 4.
The right wall is not taller, so R moves left.
Walls 8 and 6, width 1: area 6.
The right wall is not taller, so R moves left.
The answer is 49.
Time complexity is O(n) and extra space is O(1). Each step discards one wall forever, so there are at most n steps.
a1.say: Time complexity is O of n and extra space is O of one. Each step discards one wall forever, so there are at most n steps.

a1.cap: That's the Two Pointers approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
